Planning guide

Three checks before you choose

Size, material and finish decide whether millwork looks built-in or added-on. Here's how to get each one right.

Hero image
Dynamic by viewed category: Timberthane beams across a vaulted ceiling, corbels under a kitchen island overhang, shutters on a two-story facade; fallback is a mantel with crown moulding in a living room.

Hi {{ first_name|default:'there' }}, whatever you're adding, the same three decisions make it look like it was always part of the house.

Three checks

1
Size it to the space
Proportion is everything. Shutters should look like they'd cover the window if closed, corbels should suit the overhang they sit under, and beams should fit your ceiling span and spacing.
2
Match the material to the spot
Timberthane faux wood is maintenance-free. AmeriCraft is stain-grade real wood. Going outside? Tell us where and we'll steer you to the right material.
3
See it in your light
Order a material sample and hold it next to your floors, cabinets or siding at different times of day.
